stem_book: The emission spectrum of hydrogen always shows discrete bright lines rather than a continuous spread of colors. Which statement best explains this? (a) Atoms emit all possible frequencies continuously. (b) Electrons in atoms can occupy only discrete energy levels, giving fixed energy transitions. (c) Continuous radiation is absorbed by the atom. (d) Spectra arise due to interference between waves.
key: b Electrons in atoms can occupy only discrete energy levels, giving fixed energy transitions.
derived: b Electrons in atoms can occupy only discrete energy levels, giving fixed energy transitions.
correct_answer: b Electrons in atoms can occupy only discrete energy levels, giving fixed energy transitions.
work: Quantised levels ⇒ ΔE = hν takes fixed values ⇒ discrete lines
